title: Most Adults Cannot Pass This Medical Entrance Exam
summary: Ten questions test anatomy, physiology, microbiology, pharmacology and clinical safety.

landing.intro: The first questions look basic. Then the test moves into physiology, microbes and medical science most adults have forgotten.

about.body:
This ten-question entertainment challenge uses foundational medical science taught across Tier 1 English-speaking countries. It tests anatomy, physiology, cell biology, microbiology, pharmacology and infection-control basics without relying on one university’s admission syllabus.

Choose one answer for each question. Correctness stays hidden until the final reveal, where the complete answer review is available to unlock.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Answer ten increasingly difficult medical-science questions.
Choose the single most accurate answer.
Reveal your score, then unlock every answer you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not a medical-school admission exam, professional qualification, diagnosis or medical advice.

medical-q1.question: Which protein in red blood cells carries most oxygen?

medical-q2.question: In DNA, adenine normally pairs with which base?

medical-q3.question: Which organ is a major site for processing and breaking down many medicines?

medical-q4.question: Which statement best distinguishes viruses from bacteria?
answers: Viruses depend on host cells to replicate

medical-q5.question: A solution with a pH below 7 is described as what?

medical-q6.question: Which part of the autonomic nervous system is associated with 'rest and digest' activity?

medical-q7.question: Which structure prevents food from entering the airway during swallowing?

medical-q8.question: Which cranial nerve carries visual information from the eye?

medical-q9.question: Which practice is a core part of preventing infection during patient care?

medical-q10.question: What does homeostasis describe?
answers: The complete absence of change in the body
The regulation of a relatively stable internal environment
The breakdown of every medicine by the kidneys
